title: A two-pole proof of the centered pedal-area invariant
verdict: PASS for centered, signed original-side pedal area product, exactly for least periods odd or divisible by four.

native.printed: 16 October 2026, no version number on PDF

actual.support: Root checked archive content interface, reference support and independent exact controls. Independent reviewer validated all 176 manifested payloads, 142 live pins, 20 frozen Git files and the stated checker guard repair.

proof: Stachel gives the real phase advance 2v and all coprime windings. The Jacobi addition identities yield the original signed area C_A S(w) with a strictly positive coefficient. The order m of the shift mod 2K accounts correctly for odd and even N.

On the reduced torus with periods ℓ and 4iK′, the S trace has two simple poles, equal real-period residues at each contributing orbit point, and zeros half a real period away by evenness and imaginary antiperiod. Divisors then give a constant positive half-period product.

The pedal foot is an actual Euclidean projection onto complete original side lines; its bilinear meromorphic continuation has at most double poles at dn zeros and vanishes at the Jacobi poles. Pairing incident edges shrinks each foot pole to at most simple: its neighbor difference vanishes at the centered pole by parity, and no incident edge is counted twice even in period four.

A residue and antiperiod show T(u)=C_T S(u+K). Quarter-period simplification gives q_z=−αk cn/(1+dn), whose derivative yields the displayed positive residue coefficient using dn²−k²cn²=k′². Combining with the v shift gives exactly ℓ/2 modulo ℓ for odd periods and periods divisible by four; primitive periods 2 mod 4 yield a nonconstant squared elliptic trace.

Ferudun’s reflection-coordinate telescope and addition identities also express the same nonzero pedal trace and imply the coefficient. The published note explicitly credits both theorem and formula, and later arbitrary-point pole cancellation.
